title: Cassava Technologies — NVIDIA AI factory, Africa's first: US$720m programme announced 2025
description: Cassava Technologies announced on 24 March 2025 that it plans to build Africa's first AI factory — a data-centre facility powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing, deployed using NVIDIA Cloud Partner reference architectures. Strive Masiyiwa, founder and chairman, framed it as infrastructure for the AI economy that keeps data within Africa's borders; Jaap Zuiderveld, NVIDIA VP EMEA, confirmed the NCP partnership. Cassava committed to deploy at its South African data centres **by June 2025**, with expansion planned to its facilities in **Egypt, Kenya, Morocco and Nigeria**. On 7 April 2025 Bloomberg reported the programme's cost at **US$720 million**, covering roughly 12,000 NVIDIA GPUs across five regional hubs over three to four years. The South Africa hub went live in November 2025. In October 2025 NVIDIA took an equity stake in Cassava (amount undisclosed) as part of a US$150m+ equity raise for Liquid Intelligent Technologies, and STANLIB agreed a minority stake in Africa Data Centres. Primary sub-Saharan countries are ZAF, NGA and KEN; Egypt and Morocco are outside SSA.

Bond catalysed private investment (10x+ mobilisation). Supports digital connectivity across Africa.

description: USD 20 million sustainability-linked loan to WIOCC Group (via its subsidiary Open Access Data Centres / OADC) to finance expansion of core and edge data centres in the DRC, Nigeria, and South Africa. Pricing linked to energy efficiency improvements and EDGE green building certification. Co-financed with IFC (USD 10M + ZAR 200M) and RMB. Total package USD 41M.
recipient_organisation: WIOCC Group / Open Access Data Centres (OADC)

title: APC Association for Progressive Communications 2024-2027
description: Association for Progressive Communications (APC) core support 2024-2027, continuing work on internet rights, digital governance and digital inclusion. title: DDP Digital Defenders Partnership 2024-2027
description: Digital Defenders Partnership (DDP) 2024-2027 continuation, supporting digital security for civil society, journalists and human rights defenders globally including sub-Saharan Africa. Provides rapid-response digital security assistance and longer-term protective capacity for at-risk individuals and organisations.

description: SIFEM committed USD 20 million to Apis Growth Markets Fund III, a USD 500 million closed-end financial services fund targeting growth-stage opportunities in Africa, South Asia and Southeast Asia. recipient_organisation: Apis Growth Markets Fund III (AGMF III)

description: SIFEM committed USD 15 million to Helios Investors Fund V, a pan-African growth equity fund targeting mid-market companies benefiting from Africa's demographic expansion and urbanisation. The fund focuses on digital infrastructure, financial services, and tech-enabled business services, with a 50% gender equality commitment for portfolio companies.

title: timbuktoo Pan-African Start-up and Innovation Ecosystem
description: UNDP timbuktoo: pan-African innovation platform launched January 2024 at WEF Davos. Aims to mobilize $1 billion (catalytic + commercial) over 10 years to support 10,000 startups and create 10M jobs. Establishes 8 thematic hubs: Fintech (Lagos), HealthTech (Kigali), GreenTech (Nairobi), AgriTech (Accra), TradeTech (Dakar), Creatives (Cape Town), Smart Cities (Morocco), EdTech/TourismTech (Dakar). IATI shows $6.78M committed 2024-2026 for core programme operations.

description: USAID Civic DEFENDERS activity supporting civil society organizations to defend digital rights, freedom of expression online, and internet security. Covers digital safety, cybersecurity for civil society.

description: USAID Cyber Security Activity supporting cybersecurity capacity building globally including Africa. Strengthens national cybersecurity institutions, CERT teams, and cyber resilience.

title: Vernonburg: Connect One Billion Digital Invest Award
description: USAID Digital Invest award to Vernonburg supporting connectivity expansion to one billion underserved people including Africa. Private capital mobilization for internet service providers.

title: Project East2West \u2014 Pan-African Terrestrial Fibre Optic Network
description: Africa50 partnered with Bayobab (wholly owned by MTN Group) in May 2023 to co-develop Project East2West, a terrestrial fibre optic cable network supplying dark fibre and active fibre capacity across ten or more African countries, connecting landlocked countries to subsea cables on both the east and west coasts of Africa. title: Pan-African e-Commerce Initiative Panafrikanische E-Commerce Initiative
description: Context:   Electronic commerce, also known as e-commerce, is increasingly becoming an important procurement and sales channel in emerging African economies. However, key prerequisites for African companies to participate in cross-border e-commerce are not in place. Objective:   T

title: CPDIF $10M Growth Investment in 42Markets Group \u2014 Capital Markets Fintech Platform
description: Convergence Partners Digital Infrastructure Fund (CPDIF) acquired a strategic stake in 42Markets Group for $10 million in growth funding. 42Markets Group is an incubator, investor and builder of high-growth specialist businesses in the financial and capital markets sector across Africa. The company focuses on digital transformation and improved efficiency of capital markets in Africa, enabling second-tier capital markets to reduce friction and costs, improve transparency and real-time risk management across financial products, ultimately extending the reach of banking and financial services to a broader cross-section of the population. Operations span South Africa, Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana, and Mauritius.

title: DEG Investment in Partech Africa Fund II (2023)
description: DEG acquires a EUR 15 million stake in Partech Africa Fund II (PAF II), the largest African VC fund focusing on technology companies including HealthTech, FinTech, and RetailTech. The fund concentrates investments in fast-growing technology companies across Africa, including Nigeria, Egypt, South Africa, Kenya, and Senegal. TIDE II invests in young companies using tech innovations to disrupt inefficient business models in Africa. The fund is sector-agnostic and invests in market space enablement, agtech, and fintech solutions. TLcom successfully deployed TIDE Africa I across eleven investments and uses the same strategy in TIDE II. Total fund close at USD 154 million (announced April 2024).
recipient_organisation: TIDE Africa II LP / TLcom Capital

title: Digital Earth Africa Phase III
description: Funding to Geoscience Australia to support Digital Earth Africa which provides African countries with access to free and open information from satellite images relating to flooding, drought, soil and coastal erosion, agriculture, forest cover, land use and land cover change, water availability and quality, and changes to human settlements. Phase III creates additional value from Phase II by driving uptake and delivering impact at scale across 50+ African countries. Activity period 2022-07-01 to 2025-06-30.

title: African Infrastructure Investment Fund 4 \u2014 DFC $50M Equity
description: DFC equity investment of up to $50 million in African Infrastructure Investment Fund 4 (AIIF4), a closed-end infrastructure fund managed by AIIM (African Infrastructure Investment Managers) with a target of $748M. Fund invests in digital infrastructure, energy transition, and mobility/logistics across Africa. Digital component includes telecom towers (Eastcastle Infrastructure, DRC and Nigeria, wireless telecom services). Fund achieved hard cap $748M with $954M including co-investments. DFC investment supports expansion of telecommunications and digital infrastructure across Sub-Saharan Africa.
recipient_organisation: African Infrastructure Investment Fund 4 (AIIF4) / African Infrastructure Investment Managers (AIIM)

description: DFC equity investment of up to $10 million in Janngo Capital Startup Fund SLP, Africa's largest gender-equal tech VC fund, investing in early-stage innovative tech startups primarily in Francophone West Africa (Côte d'Ivoire, Senegal). recipient_organisation: Janngo Capital Startup Fund SLP / Janngo Capital Partners SAS

description: Wehubit 2.0 builds on the Wehubit 1.0 programme (2018-2023) to continue identifying and supporting scaling of digital and green social innovations in the public and non-profit sectors. description: FCDO grant to the Open Government Partnership to promote open and accountable use of emerging digital technologies, especially ensuring democratic safeguards for AI and automation. Translates global pledges into country-level action. Supports digital governance reforms in priority countries: Ghana, Indonesia, Kenya, Nigeria, Dominican Republic. Investments represent 15.6% of Group revenue.

description: Finnfund EUR 12 million parallel loan to Wave Mobile Money, a low-cost mobile money platform providing affordable deposit, withdrawal and payment services in West Africa. Wave operates in LDC countries with very low banking penetration, offering free deposit/withdrawal services to increase financial inclusion.
recipient_organisation: Wave Mobile Money S.A. / Wave Côte d'Ivoire S.A.

title: Partech Africa Fund II SSA Tech Startup VC Fund
description: FMO equity commitment of EUR 25M to Partech Africa Fund II, a generalist tech venture capital fund targeting early-stage fintech, mobile consumer services, mobility, supply chain, and digital economy startups in Sub-Saharan Africa. Fund closed at EUR 263M/USD 300M+ with KfW as anchor.

title: COMESA MSME focused Digital Real Time Retail Payment Platform (Phase III)
description: this investment will be used to support the COMESA Business Council to deploy a pro-poor instant and inclusive digital payment system and  scheme rules/standards that will serve the payment needs of MSME's in COMESA region in Africa

title: Axian Telecom Bond \u2014 IFC Anchor Investor
description: IFC acted as anchor investor in Axian Telecom's debut bond issuance, committing $60 million from its own account. Axian Telecom is a pan-African telecommunications and digital infrastructure company operating in Madagascar, Tanzania, Togo, Senegal, Comoros, and Réunion. The bond — total size approximately €430 million — finances network expansion, spectrum acquisition, and mobile money infrastructure across Axian's SSA markets. IFC's anchor participation was intended to attract market investors at a time of financial market volatility. BII and other DFIs co-participated.

title: Airtel Africa Mobile Internet Connectivity Expansion (2022)
description: IFC committed $150 million from its own account plus $44 million from the Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program (MCPP) — a total of $194 million — to Airtel Africa to support expansion of mobile internet connectivity across six Sub-Saharan African countries: DRC, Kenya, Madagascar, Niger, Republic of Congo, and Zambia. Airtel Africa is one of the continent's leading mobile network operators. The financing enables rollout of 4G networks, upgrading of existing infrastructure, and expansion into underserved rural and peri-urban areas, directly contributing to affordable mobile internet access for millions of users.

title: WIOCC Group Equity Investment \u2014 Data Centres and Fibre (2022)
description: IFC made a $30 million equity investment in WIOCC Holding Company Ltd (WHCL), the restructured parent of WIOCC, to support expansion of core and edge data centres and fibre networks in DRC, Nigeria, and South Africa. WIOCC's Open Access Data Centres (OADC) strategy targets Tier III data centres across Africa serving cloud providers, enterprises, and internet exchanges. The IFC equity stake aligns with WIOCC's $200M combined debt and equity raise in 2021-2022 to fund the OADC strategy. Proparco, EAAIF (Ninety-One), and other DFIs also participated.
recipient_organisation: WIOCC Group (WIOCC Holding Company Ltd / Open Access Data Centres)

title: Wave Mobile Money \u2014 IFC Debt Facility (Senegal + C\u00f4te d'Ivoire)
description: IFC provided a senior debt facility of €25 million (A-loan) to Wave Mobile Money S.A. (Senegal entity) and Wave Côte d'Ivoire S.A. as part of a €130 million total financing package. Wave is Francophone Africa's first fintech unicorn ($1.7B valuation), operating a low-cost interoperable mobile money platform across Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, Burkina Faso, Gambia, Mali, Niger, and Uganda. IFC's participation mobilised €65M in B-loans from impact lenders (Symbiotics, BlueOrchard, responsAbility, Lendable). Proparco/Finnfund/Norfund provided €24M in parallel loans. Total €130M package.
recipient_organisation: Wave Mobile Money S.A. (Senegal) / Wave Côte d'Ivoire S.A.

title: M-KOPA Connected Asset Financing \u2014 IFC Senior Debt Facility
description: IFC committed senior secured loans to M-KOPA: up to $50 million (or KES equivalent) to M-KOPA Kenya Limited and up to $15 million (or UGX equivalent) to M-KOPA Uganda Limited. M-KOPA is Africa's leading connected asset financing provider, offering smartphones, solar home systems, and digital financial services (cash loans, mobile insurance) to over-indebted, underserved households through a pay-as-you-go (PAYG) model using mobile money instalments. Approved December 2022 and invested February 2023. IFC is a principal debt financier alongside BII which also holds equity and debt positions.
recipient_organisation: M-KOPA Kenya Limited / M-KOPA Uganda Limited

title: Partech Africa Fund II \u2014 IFC LP Commitment
description: IFC committed up to €25 million (~$26.3M) as a limited partner in Partech Africa Fund II (PAF II), an early-stage venture capital fund investing in Seed to Series D technology businesses across Africa. Partech Africa II reached final close above €300 million in 2024. Co-LPs include BII ($15.6M), KfW, EIB, DEG, FMO, Proparco, Mubadala, and Bpifrance. The fund targets fintech, logistics, digital health, e-commerce, and digital infrastructure companies. Portfolio includes Wave (mobile money), Maad Africa, Revio Pay, Foondamate, and others across 27+ African countries.

title: Symbiotics Africa Multi-Currency Impact Bond for Financial Inclusion
description: IFU partnered with Symbiotics to provide USD 22.5 million in debt financing to 15-20 financial institutions in Sub-Saharan Africa through a multi-currency impact bond. The bond finances loans to businesses and households via digital-enabled microfinance institutions and SME banks, supporting financial inclusion and economic recovery post-COVID.

title: Fonds f\u00fcr Digitale Transformation Westafrika
description: Die öffentlichen Verwaltungen Westafrikas haben einen hohen Modernisierungsbedarf, um die SDGs zu erreichen. Denn eine zentrale Voraussetzung zur Verbesserung der Regierungsführung in Afrika ist deren digitale Transformation: Durch die Digitalisierung der Verwaltung und Automatisierung ihrer Prozesse können die Kosten reduziert, Effizienz und Transparenz erhöht werden. Eine digitale Verwaltung kann damit entscheidend dazu beitragen, die Korruption zu senken und die Rechenschaftspflicht der Regie

title: Mastercard Foundation Africa Growth Fund \u2014 $200M Fund-of-Funds
description: MCF $200M fund-of-funds launched December 2022 to catalyse risk capital through African-owned and led investment vehicles with gender-lens investing. Invests in VC and SME funds targeting women-led enterprises across Ethiopia, Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda, Senegal and Uganda. Target: 15,000 direct jobs. Portfolio includes Aruwa Capital, Inua Capital, Chui Ventures, VestedWorld, SME Impact Fund, Sabou Capital and others.
recipient_organisation: Mastercard Foundation Africa Growth Fund / MEDA

title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program \u2014 Digital and Leadership Track (2022 tranche)
description: MCF Scholars Program committed $1.7B over first decade (2012-2022) to nearly 40,000 scholars. Target 100,000 scholars by 2030 across 33 partner institutions in Africa. Primarily serves SSA countries. Digital focus includes technology and engineering degrees at CMU-Africa, AIMS, and partner institutions. University of Rwanda 10-year $55M partnership also included.

title: AfricaGrow LP commitment to TLcom TIDE Africa Fund II
description: AfricaGrow (through Allianz and DEG Impact joint vehicle) commits to TLcom Capital's TIDE Africa Fund II, Africa's largest early-stage VC fund at $154M final close. Fund targets seed and Series A across East and West Africa (Nigeria, Kenya, Egypt, South Africa). Digital focus: fintech, agritech, healthtech, logistics. First close $70M in Jan 2022, final close April 2024.

title: Wave Mobile Money \u2014 EUR 90M Syndicated Debt Facility
description: Norfund EUR 12 million parallel bilateral loan in EUR 90 million IFC-led syndicated debt facility for Wave Mobile Money. Wave provides low-cost mobile wallet, transfers, and merchant payment services in Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, Gambia, Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger. Pure-play mobile money unicorn in Francophone West Africa. Digital scope: mobile money platform, digital payments, financial inclusion.

title: Orange MEA Annual Network CapEx Programme 2022 (SSA portion)
description: Orange invested over €1 billion in 2022 across its MEA region for network deployment including 4G/5G rollout, fibre extension, and mobile broadband across SSA countries including Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, Cameroon, Mali, Burkina Faso, Guinea, Madagascar, DRC, Liberia, Sierra Leone.

title: Axian Telecom Bond - EAIF Anchor Investment
description: EAIF was an anchor investor in bond issuances by Axian Telecom, a pan-African telecommunications and digital company. First investment: USD 20M in the February 2022 bond (total USD 420M raised) to fund telecom expansion. Second tranche: USD 30M commitment in 2023 bond. Axian operates in Madagascar, Togo, Tanzania, Uganda, Senegal, Comoros and other markets.

title: Sun King (Greenlight Planet) \u2014 Green Bond for Off-Grid Solar PAYG in Sub-Saharan Africa
description: USD 10 million subscription to a green bond arranged by Symbiotics Investments and on-lent to Sun King (Greenlight Planet / GLP), a leading off-grid solar kit provider in SSA. Proceeds support distribution of solar home systems and lanterns with digital pay-as-you-go (PAYG) financing via mobile money. Sun King is one of the world's largest off-grid solar PAYG providers in SSA.

title: Accion Digital Transformation Fund (Africa fintech)
description: Accion Digital Transformation Fund 2022-2032, a private debt impact investment fund providing finance to financial institutions and fintech companies in Africa. Supports digital financial infrastructure, agent networks and mobile money platforms to expand access to formal financial services for underserved populations across sub-Saharan Africa.

title: SPIDER Phase-out Support 2022-2024
description: Phase-out support for SPIDER (Swedish Programme for ICT in Developing Regions) at Stockholm University covering 2022-2024. SSA countries include Kenya, Uganda, South Africa and Zambia. Supports knowledge transfer and closure activities for the long-running ICT capacity programme.

title: Cathay AfricInvest Innovation Fund I \u2014 SIFEM
description: SIFEM committed EUR 7 million to Cathay AfricInvest Innovation Fund I (CAIF I), a €110 million pan-African venture capital fund jointly managed by AfricInvest and Cathay Innovation. The fund invests in innovative African tech companies across software, financial services, communications, healthcare and education, supporting digital entrepreneurship and financial innovation across SSA.
recipient_organisation: Cathay AfricInvest Innovation Fund I (CAIF I)

title: Convergence Partners Digital Infrastructure Fund (CPDIF) \u2014 SIFEM
description: SIFEM committed USD 15 million to the Convergence Partners Digital Infrastructure Fund (CPDIF), a USD 296 million fund investing in digital infrastructure and digital services companies across Sub-Saharan Africa. The fund bridges the digital divide in SSA by investing in fibre networks, data centres, cloud infrastructure and telecom platforms.
recipient_organisation: Convergence Partners Digital Infrastructure Fund LP

title: Lendable MSME Fintech Credit Fund \u2014 SIFEM
description: SIFEM committed USD 10 million to the Lendable MSME Fintech Credit Fund, a USD 110 million fintech debt fund providing senior-secured debt to early and mid-stage fintech companies across Africa and Asia. The fund supports digital financial inclusion by enabling fintech lenders providing consumer and MSME credit, payments, and remittances to underbanked populations in Africa.

title: Accion Digital Transformation Fund
description: Swedfund invested up to USD 15 million in the Accion Digital Transformation Fund, focused on the digital transformation of financial institutions in developing countries in Africa and South and Southeast Asia. Accion supports digital transformation through capital, strategic and technical advice and governance support to microfinance institutions and financial service providers. The fund raised USD 152.5 million in its 2024 close with co-investors BII, FMO, IFC, Mastercard, and OeEB.

title: TIDE Africa Fund II
description: Swedfund invested USD 10 million in TIDE Africa Fund II, a venture capital fund by TLcom Capital dedicated to financing scalable and innovative digital business models in Africa. The fund supports tech entrepreneurs building digital solutions from local needs in Africa, contributing to increased digitalisation, digital inclusion and economic growth. Portfolio companies operate in Nigeria, Kenya, Egypt and South Africa.

amount_quality: multi-year aggregate; anchor commitment, partially overlapping separately-held sub-components
title: Google — US$1 billion Africa digital transformation commitment, 2021–2026
description: Google CEO Sundar Pichai announced at Google for Africa on 6 October 2021 a US$1 billion investment over five years to support Africa's digital transformation, covering: (1) affordable connectivity, including the Equiano subsea cable, which landed in Nigeria, Namibia, Togo, South Africa and São Tomé and Príncipe; (2) building products for African users; (3) investing in entrepreneurs via a US$50 million Africa Investment Fund and the Black Founders Fund; (4) supporting non-profits (US$40 million) and SME lending (US$10 million via Kiva). Named countries include NGA, ZAF, KEN, GHA, UGA, NAM, TGO and STP.

title: Africa Data Centres \u2014 $500 Million Pan-African Data Centre Build-Out Programme
description: In September 2021, Africa Data Centres (ADC), a subsidiary of Cassava Technologies (formerly Liquid Intelligent Technologies), announced a $500 million investment programme to build 10 interconnected, cloud- and carrier-neutral data centres across 10 African countries over two years, doubling its existing footprint. The programme is financed through a combination of debt and equity, including a $300 million DFC direct loan (committed 2020, first disbursement Aug 2022 for South Africa), corporate equity from Cassava Technologies/ADC, and local debt facilities. Target countries include South Africa (Johannesburg JHB1, JHB2, Cape Town CPT1, CPT2), Kenya (Nairobi NBO1, NBO2), Nigeria (Lagos LOS1), Ghana (Accra ACC1), Togo (Lomé), and others. As of 2024, ADC has spent the $500M and operates facilities from South Africa to West Africa.

title: Eastcastle Infrastructure \u2014 Consortium Equity Investment (Adenia Stake)
description: Adenia Partners, together with African Infrastructure Investment Managers (AIIM) and IFC, invested a total of USD 130 million in Eastcastle Infrastructure Limited, a newly established telecom tower developer in Africa. Eastcastle was founded in 2020 by former Eaton Towers CFO and COO. The consortium holds 95.8% of Eastcastle (AIIM 37.9%, Adenia 37.9%, IFC 20%, founders 4.2%). Funds support a build-to-suit strategy to develop new telecom towers for 3G/4G/5G deployment in the Democratic Republic of Congo, Nigeria, and Côte d'Ivoire. Adenia's committed share is approximately $49.3 million (37.9% of $130M total).

title: Multinational - Institutional Support for Digital Payments and e-Commerce Policies for Cross-Border Trade (IDECT)
description: The proposed project is an institutional Support for Digital Payments and e-Commerce Policies for Cross-border Trade (IDECT). It will be financed with an ADF-15 Regional Public Good grant and the Executing Agency is the Smart Africa Secretariat. This project proposes to address key policy gaps to un...

title: Multinational - ICT Cybersecurity (R&D, FINTECH and DFS)
description: A grant of UA 1,503,895 (approximately USD 2,166,000) from ADFI for research and development in ICT cybersecurity, fintech, and digital financial services. Approved February 2021. Aimed at building cybersecurity capacity for digital financial services ecosystem in Africa.

title: AfricInvest FIVE co-leads $100M Series C for MFS Africa pan-African digital payments network
description: AfricInvest's Financial Inclusion Vehicle (FIVE) co-leads a USD 100 million Series C financing round (USD 70M equity + USD 30M debt) for MFS Africa, Africa's largest digital payments network and interoperability hub. Round co-led with existing investors Goodwell Investments and LUN Partners, alongside CommerzVentures, Allan Gray Ventures and Endeavour. MFS Africa connects mobile network operators across 40+ African markets through a single API, enabling mobile money interoperability and cross-border digital payments. AfricInvest also participated in the USD 100M Series C extension in 2022.

title: Convergence Partners Digital Infrastructure Fund \u2014 LP Investment
description: BII committed $40M total to the Convergence Partners Digital Infrastructure Fund (CPDIF), a specialist SSA digital infrastructure fund managed by Convergence Partners. Investment 1: $30M (Jul 2021). Investment 2: $10M top-up (Jun 2022). The fund invests in digital infrastructure across Sub-Saharan Africa including data centres, fibre networks, broadband connectivity, and tech-enabled services. Portfolio companies include: 42Markets (SA digital trading), C Squared InvestCo (fibre/data Mauritius), CTrack Africa (fleet telematics), Datacentrix (data centre SA), Merit HoldCo (Nigeria digital infrastructure), Yellow Digital Retailers (device financing: Madagascar, Malawi, Rwanda, Uganda, Zambia).

financier: Belgian Investment Company for Developing Countries
title: Cathay Africinvest Innovation Fund \u2014 Pan-African Venture Capital
description: EUR 6M (two tranches: EUR 4M in 2021 + EUR 2M follow-on) equity in Cathay AfricInvest Innovation Fund (CAIF), a pan-African VC fund. CAIF reached €110M final close in 2023, co-managed by AfricInvest and Cathay Innovation. Invests in digital tech companies from seed to growth stage across Africa (Egypt, Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa). Focus on digital economy, fintech, healthtech, edtech, and agritech startups with scaling potential.

title: Liquid Intelligent Technologies USD 620 Million Bond \u2014 Fibre and Data Centre Expansion (2021)
description: In February 2021, Liquid Telecommunications Financing PLC (a subsidiary of Liquid Intelligent Technologies, itself owned by Cassava Technologies) issued a USD 620 million bond oversubscribed 5x. Bond proceeds used to refinance existing debt and fund new fibre infrastructure, data centres, and new technologies across Liquid's 14+ SSA country network (ZAF, ZWE, ZMB, KEN, TZA, COD, UGA, RWA, BWA, ETH, MOZ, LSO, SSD, plus cross-border links). Liquid's network at issuance spanned approximately 100,000 km of fibre. DFI anchor investors: IFC USD 150M (bond) + USD 90M (equity) + USD 100M (ZAF term loan), DEG USD 25M, EAIF/PIDG USD 9.77M. This records the Cassava/Liquid corporate issuance.
recipient_organisation: Liquid Telecommunications Holdings Ltd / Liquid Intelligent Technologies (Cassava subsidiary)

title: DEG Anchor Investment in Liquid Telecommunications USD 620M Bond (2021)
description: DEG invests USD 25 million as anchor investor in the USD 620 million bond issued by Liquid Telecommunications Financing PLC, part of the pan-African telecoms group Liquid Intelligent Technologies (owned by Econet Global). The bond was the first Liquid Telecom capital market issuance since 2017 and was oversubscribed 5x. Liquid Telecommunications operates Africa's largest multi-country fibre optic network across Sub-Saharan Africa including South Africa, Zimbabwe, Zambia, Kenya, Tanzania, DRC, and Botswana, also operating Africa Data Centres (ADC) as a subsidiary. Proceeds used to refinance existing debt and fund growth including new fibre infrastructure, data centres, and new technologies.
recipient_organisation: Liquid Telecommunications Holdings / Liquid Intelligent Technologies

title: Convergence Partners Digital Infrastructure Fund \u2014 DFC $25M Equity
description: DFC equity investment of up to $25 million in Convergence Partners Digital Infrastructure Fund (CPDIF), a specialist Africa-focused ICT private equity fund. The fund invests in optical fibre installations, wireless towers, data centres, cloud, IoT, and AI infrastructure across sub-Saharan Africa. First close July 2021 at $120M; final close $296M. Portfolio companies include CSquared (Kenya broadband). DFC share is up to $25M out of $296M fund. Target countries: DRC, Ethiopia, Côte d'Ivoire, Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, South Africa.
recipient_organisation: Convergence Partners Digital Infrastructure Fund L.P. / Convergence Partners Africa

title: Lendable MSME Fintech Credit Fund \u2014 DFC $20M Loan
description: DFC direct loan of up to $20 million to Lendable Fintech Credit Fund (Luxembourg RAIF), providing senior-secured debt facilities to early and mid-stage fintech companies operating in Africa (Kenya, Uganda, Nigeria, Ghana, South Africa, Senegal) and Asia. Lendable's data-driven approach enables on-lending to digital financial service providers serving underbanked MSMEs. DFC is an anchor investor. Total fund $110M. Promotes financial inclusion through digital lending platforms.
recipient_organisation: Lendable Inc. / Lendable Fintech Credit Fund

financier: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Netherlands
title: Develop Digital Trade Competitiveness In Selected African Countries
description: Programme to develop digital trade competitiveness of services sectors in selected African countries. Focuses on e-commerce, digital services exports, and trade facilitation in support of inclusive economic growth and AfCFTA.

title: Digital Health for COVID-19
description: Support to the deployment of digital health tools for COVID-19 tools deployment in Sub-Saharan Africa

title: Investments on regional infrastructures
description: Development of resilient continental/inter-regional infrastructure for transport multimodal networks, energy networks and digital networks via blended finance, feasibility studies and support to Sub-Saharan African Transport Policy Program

title: DATAFID \u2014 Regional Project to Support Strengthening of Digital Economy Statistics and Use of Data Science by Tax and Customs Administrations
description: DATAFID aims to increase knowledge about the digital economy and its impacts, and to build the capacities of tax and customs administrations through improved use of data science. Two components: (1) improving knowledge of the digital economy to include it in the tax system; (2) improving the transparency and performance of tax and customs administrations. Beneficiary countries: Cameroon, Côte d'Ivoire, Niger, Senegal, Togo (Component 1); Côte d'Ivoire, Mauritania, Niger, Togo (Component 2). Implemented with AFRISTAT, INSEE, FERDI. Financed by the French Directorate-General of the Treasury (DG Trésor) under the Strategic Investment Plan for Development (PISD) 2020–2023.
recipient_organisation: AFRISTAT; INSEE; FERDI; national tax and customs administrations

title: UK Digital Access Programme (DAP) \u2014 Multi-country
description: The Digital Access Programme (DAP) is a FCDO-DCMS joint programme catalysing more inclusive, affordable, safe and secure digital access for excluded and underserved communities in Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa, Brazil and Indonesia. Components include: (1) Support to inclusive connectivity, digital skills, content and services for underserved communities (delivered via KPMG-led consortium); (2) Technical assistance on policy, legal and regulatory frameworks for digital inclusion; (3) Programme management and advisory. Achieved reach of 10.2 million people across all five countries. Cybersecurity capacity building (Pillar 2) funded separately under Africa Cyber Programme. Commit and disbursement figures represent IATI-reported FCDO share, SSA-attributable portion (KE/NG/ZA = 3/5).
recipient_organisation: Governments/implementing partners in Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa (plus Brazil, Indonesia outside SSA)

title: Google Africa Investment Fund \u2014 $50M Equity Fund
description: Google established the $50 million Africa Investment Fund at Google for Africa 2021 to make equity investments in early- and growth-stage African technology startups. The fund provides equity capital plus access to Google technology, employees, and networks. Initial portfolio (as of 2022): SafeBoda (Uganda, mobility super-app), Carry1st (South Africa, mobile gaming), Lori Systems (Kenya, logistics). Individual ticket sizes are not publicly disclosed.
recipient_organisation: Growth-stage African tech startups (SafeBoda, Carry1st, Lori Systems, and others)

title: Google for Startups Black Founders Fund Africa \u2014 2021-2023 Cohorts
description: Google's non-dilutive Black Founders Fund Africa provided equity-free cash grants to Black-led African startups. Cohort 1 (2021): $3 million to 50 startups ($50K-$100K each). Cohort 2 (2022): $4 million to 60 startups. Subsequent cohorts add further tranches. Total $7+ million disbursed to 110 African startups by end of 2023, as reported by Google in December 2023. Each recipient also receives $200K in Google Cloud Credits.

title: Google-Kiva Low-Interest SME Loans Africa \u2014 $10M Partnership
description: As part of the $1 billion Africa commitment (October 2021), Google pledged $10 million in partnership with Kiva to provide low-interest loans to small and medium-sized businesses in Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, and South Africa. The programme enables SMEs to access affordable credit to grow their digital businesses.
recipient_organisation: Small and medium-sized businesses via Kiva

title: Google Africa Nonprofit Support \u2014 $40M Commitment 2021-2026
description: As part of the $1 billion Africa commitment, Google pledged $40 million in cash and in-kind support to nonprofits improving lives across Africa over five years. Confirmed in October 2022 progress report. Includes a $3 million grant to AirQo (Uganda) for air quality monitoring expansion. Supports nonprofits working on digital inclusion, health, education, and economic development.
recipient_organisation: Nonprofits and NGOs working across Africa including AirQo

title: Liquid Telecom Bond \u2014 IFC Anchor Bond Investment
description: IFC acted as anchor investor in Liquid Telecom Holdings Ltd's senior unsecured bond issuance, providing $150 million from its own account. Liquid Intelligent Technologies is the largest independent pan-African fibre and data centre operator, with a network spanning 14+ SSA countries including Kenya, South Africa, Zimbabwe, Zambia, Rwanda, Uganda, and DRC. Proceeds finance expansion of fibre optic network and data centre capacity across Sub-Saharan Africa. The bond was part of a broader IFC engagement with Liquid including a separate equity investment and South Africa term loan totalling over $250 million.
recipient_organisation: Liquid Intelligent Technologies (Liquid Telecom Holdings Ltd)

title: Liquid Telecom Equity Investment \u2014 Pan-SSA Data Centres
description: IFC made a $90 million equity investment in Liquid Telecom Jersey Ltd, the holding entity for Liquid's data centre operations across Sub-Saharan Africa. Liquid Intelligent Technologies is the largest independent data centre operator in SSA, with facilities in South Africa, Kenya, Zimbabwe, Zambia, and elsewhere. The investment accelerates expansion of cloud-hosting, colocation, and internet exchange point services. Co-investors in the Cassava Technologies platform include BII (British International Investment), US DFC, FinnFund, Google, Public Investment Corporation (South Africa), and others.
recipient_organisation: Liquid Telecom Jersey Ltd (Cassava Technologies data centre entity)

title: Convergence Partners Digital Infrastructure Fund \u2014 IFC LP Investment
description: IFC committed $25 million as a limited partner in the Convergence Partners Digital Infrastructure Fund (CPDIF), a specialist Sub-Saharan African digital infrastructure fund managed by Convergence Partners, targeting $250 million in commitments. CPDIF invests in digital infrastructure across SSA including data centres, fibre networks, broadband connectivity, tech-enabled services, and digital platforms. Portfolio includes CSquared (fibre/data Mauritius), Datacentrix (SA data centre), Merit HoldCo (Nigeria digital infrastructure), Yellow Digital Retailers (device financing across 6 SSA countries). Co-investors: BII ($40M), Proparco, DEG, and others.

title: Boosting Digital Skills Through Digital Transformation Centres (DTCs)
description: Norway/Norad-funded ITU project (CHF 3.77M total) to boost digital skills through Digital Transformation Centres. Supports 12 countries globally; 6 SSA: DR Congo Ghana Cote d'Ivoire Rwanda Uganda Zambia. Delivers basic and intermediate digital skills training especially for rural and underserved communities; curriculum development; trainer training. Builds on ITU-Cisco DTC Initiative launched September 2019. Norad contribution CHF 3.0M; ITU ICT-DF CHF 759K. Phase 2 continuation project 9GLO23133.

title: Verdant Capital Hybrid Fund Verdant Capital Hybrid Fund
description: Der Verdant Capital Hybrid Fund (VCHF) zielt darauf ab, (Mikro-) Finanzinstitutionen, kleinere Banken, Fintech-, Leasing- und Factoring-Unternehmen in Afrika Hybridkapital zur Verfügung zu stellen. title: Bpifrance-Mubadala Africa Co-Investment Partnership (Mubadala share)
description: Mubadala Investment Company's half of the EUR 350 million Africa co-investment partnership announced jointly with French public investment bank Bpifrance on 30 June 2021 at the 13th UAE-France Strategic Dialogue. The MoU commits both parties to deploy capital through fund and direct investments in high-growth African startups, SMEs and mid-cap companies across regional, multi-country and pan-African private equity and venture capital funds. Mubadala's indicative share is half (~EUR 175M) of the stated EUR 350M total objective; the split is not explicitly 50/50 in official sources but no other split has been disclosed. First deployment under this partnership: Partech Africa II (March 2024).

title: AktivCo Solar Solarisation of Telecom Towers \u2014 West and Central Africa
description: Norfund EUR 9 million in EUR 60 million credit facility (FEI lead EUR 27M + Proparco EUR 6M + Norfund EUR 9M + AfricaGoGreen EUR 8M) for AktivCo, Camusat Group's Africa energy services subsidiary. Deploys solar+battery hybrid power at approximately 3,000 telecom tower sites in Chad, Niger, Cameroon, Côte d'Ivoire, Burkina Faso. Enables cleaner, more reliable mobile connectivity across SSA.

title: Baobab+ Solar Home Systems and Digital Inclusion \u2014 West Africa and Madagascar
description: Norfund EUR 10 million equity in Baobab+, leading solar home systems distributor in West Africa and Madagascar. Baobab+ bundles solar kits with digital tablets and mobile financial services for off-grid households in Côte d'Ivoire, Mali, Senegal, Madagascar. Planned expansion to Nigeria and DRC. Digital scope: solar-digital product bundle (solar + tablet), digital financial inclusion, mobile payment collection, digital literacy.

title: Orange Digital Centres SSA Network - Digital Skills and Startup Incubation
description: Orange's network of Orange Digital Centres (ODCs) in SSA provides free digital skills training, startup incubation (Orange Fab accelerator), and maker spaces. SSA countries covered include Senegal (Dakar - 2nd ODC 2019, ODC Champions), Côte d'Ivoire, Cameroon, Madagascar, Botswana, DRC, Mali, Burkina Faso, Guinea, Sierra Leone. In 2023, ODC Summer Challenge ran across 11 countries, ODC Champions across 15 countries. Orange Cameroun invested XOF 1.5 billion in its ODCs as of 2025.

title: Liquid Telecom Bond - EAIF Anchor Investment
description: EAIF anchored the bond issuance of Liquid Telecom to fund expansion of its pan-African telecom business. Liquid Telecom (now Liquid Intelligent Technologies) is a major fibre, cloud and broadband provider across 13+ African countries including DRC, Zambia, Zimbabwe, South Africa, Kenya, Uganda, Rwanda, Tanzania, Ethiopia, Mozambique, Botswana, Lesotho and South Sudan.

title: Africa Mobile Network (AMN) \u2014 Rural Telecom Tower Deployment Sub-Saharan Africa
description: EUR 8 million equity investment in Africa Mobile Network (AMN), a pan-SSA telecom company deploying towers in rural areas. Financing supports deployment of 5,000 new towers by 2022 and expansion to 10,000 towers across 19+ African countries by 2025, bridging the digital divide in rural SSA. Total consortium USD 40 million (Proparco, CDC, DEG, Metier PE).

title: d.light \u2014 Off-Grid Solar with Digital Pay-As-You-Go Access (Kenya, Nigeria, Tanzania, Uganda)
description: USD 10 million equity investment in d.light, a leading off-grid solar kit provider operating a digital pay-as-you-go (PAYG) model in SSA. d.light uses mobile money and digital payment infrastructure to extend solar energy access to unelectrified households. The PAYG model is built on digital financial services. Operations in Kenya, Nigeria, Tanzania, Uganda.

title: GSMA 2021-2024 (Mobile for Development)
description: Sida core grant to GSMA Mobile for Development (M4D) programme 2021-2024, supporting mobile internet connectivity and digital inclusion across low- and middle-income countries. SSA beneficiary countries include Ghana, Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda. Co-financed with FCDO.

title: Privacy International 2021-2026 (Data Privacy and Rights)
description: Privacy International core support 2021-2026 for data privacy and digital rights advocacy. Investigates and challenges data exploitation, surveillance and privacy violations globally including Africa. Supports civil society capacity to challenge intrusive data practices and advocate for effective data protection laws.

title: Reimagine Education \u2014 Airtel Africa Partnership: Digital Learning for Schools Across SSA
description: UNICEF's Reimagine Education initiative (launched 2020) calls for public and private sector investment in digital learning as an essential service for every child. Airtel Africa, the first African private sector partner, committed USD 57 million over 5 years (2021-2027) to UNICEF's Reimagine Education initiative to connect schools across 13 African countries (Chad, Congo, DRC, Gabon, Kenya, Madagascar, Malawi, Niger, Nigeria, Rwanda, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia) to the internet and provide free access to learning platforms. By end 2023, 1,500+ schools connected, 17,000 teachers trained, reaching nearly 1 million learners across 13 countries. By March 2026, 3,296 schools cumulative. UNICEF provides technical leadership, digital content (Learning Passport), and zero-rated platform access. Airtel provides network infrastructure and financial contribution.

title: Critical Infrastructure Digitalization and Resilience (CIDR)
description: USAID Critical Infrastructure Digitalization and Resilience program strengthening security and resilience of critical digital infrastructure including energy and communications systems.

title: Cyber Workforce
description: USAID program building cybersecurity workforce capacity in Africa and globally. Supports development of cyber professionals, CERT/CSIRT teams, and national cyber capacity.

title: Digital Invest - Integra Partners (Digital Finance)
description: USAID Digital Invest activity with Integra Partners supporting digital financial services and fintech investment globally including Africa. Mobilizes private capital for fintech infrastructure.

title: Lendable MSME Fintech Credit Fund
description: USAID Digital Invest activity supporting Lendable's fintech credit fund for MSMEs. Mobilizes private capital for fintech-enabled lending platforms including Africa.

title: Multinational - Artificial Intelligence-enabled financial complaints management for central banks in Africa
description: A grant of UA 769,994 (approximately USD 1,094,000) from ADFI for AI-enabled financial complaints management systems for central banks across Africa. Approved December 2020. Supports deployment of AI for financial services regulation and consumer protection.

title: Liquid Intelligent Technologies \u2014 Follow-on Equity (Data Centres)
description: Follow-on $40M equity investment by BII in Liquid Telecommunications Jersey Limited in July 2020, to enhance and expand Liquid's data centre business across Sub-Saharan Africa. Liquid Telecom is the largest independent data centre operator in Sub-Saharan Africa, operating facilities in Johannesburg, Nairobi, Harare, Lusaka and elsewhere. This investment supports cloud hosting, colocation services, and internet exchange points across SSA, directly enabling digital infrastructure for businesses.
recipient_organisation: Liquid Telecommunications Jersey Limited (Cassava Technologies data centre business)

financier: Belgian Investment Company for Developing Countries
title: TIDE Africa Fund (TLcom) \u2014 Tech Venture Capital
description: EUR 4.37M (USD 5M) equity in TLcom TIDE Africa Fund, a venture capital fund exclusively focused on technology-enabled services and innovation for sub-Saharan Africa. Fund reached USD 71M final close in February 2020. Invests across the VC cycle in fast-growth digital tech companies serving SSA markets. Co-investors include IFC and South Africa's Sango Capital. Portfolio companies include Andela, Twiga Foods, ULesson. Primary focus countries: Kenya, Nigeria.

title: Inclusive and harmonized digital and data policies in Africa Inklusive und harmonisierte Digital- und Datenpolitiken in Afrika
description: Context:   To date, many African countries have only profited little in the prosperity gains resulting from digital transformation. There is a lack of digital infrastructure and skills, as well as a shortage of financial resources. In addition, a digital divide exists between African countries, as well as between women and men. This gap in terms of access to digital technologies further limits the participation of those affected. Regulatory conditions pose an obstacle to the development of inclu

title: DEG Anchor Investment in Helios Towers USD 750M Senior Bond (2020)
description: DEG acts as anchor investor in the USD 750 million senior bond issued by HTA Group Ltd, a subsidiary of Helios Towers plc, Africa's leading independent telecommunications tower company. The bond, the second in Helios Towers' corporate history, was one of the first capital market issuances by a private-sector company from a developing country since the COVID-19 pandemic outbreak. Helios Towers operates over 7,000 telecommunications towers in Tanzania, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Ghana, Congo Brazzaville, and South Africa, serving multiple mobile network operators. Proceeds used for tower expansion and operational growth.
recipient_organisation: Helios Towers PLC / HTA Group Ltd

title: Africa Data Centres \u2014 DFC $300M Data Centre Loan
description: DFC direct loan of up to $300 million to Africa Data Centres Holdings Limited under a master finance agreement to finance the acquisition and expansion of existing data center assets in South Africa and Kenya, and entry into new markets through development, construction, and operation of carrier-neutral data centers across DFC-eligible African countries. First disbursement of $83M announced August 2022 primarily for South Africa expansion. Africa Data Centres is Africa's largest network of interconnected data facilities. Total project cost $428.6M. Supports seven existing and greenfield data centers in five countries.
recipient_organisation: Africa Data Centres Holdings Limited / Cassava Technologies

financier: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Netherlands
title: World Bank Digital Development Partnership COVID-19 Emergency Response
description: Dutch contribution to the World Bank Digital Development Partnership emergency response work program during COVID-19. Aims to secure the digital sector and support developing countries in maintaining digital infrastructure during the pandemic.

title: EU digital solutions to strengthen the resilience of education and health systems to COVID-19 in the Eastern, Southern Africa and Indian Ocean Region
